A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CityWalker and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C. Corresponding methods and experiments can be matched reliably across the revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original offline navigation benchmarks, real-world Go1 trials, scaling experiments, and ablations, including a 77.3% overall CityWalker success rate in Table 2.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results and adds backbone/architecture comparisons and inference-speed measurements in Appendix B.

M1.justification: V3 adds evaluated encoder variants using EfficientNetB0, ResNet50, and ACO-pretrained ResNet34, presenting EfficientNetB0 as a faster deployment option. The default DINOv2 model, DPVO labeling pipeline, transformer, prediction heads, and losses remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same walking/driving video sources, New York City teleoperation data, critical scenarios, and real-world Go1 navigation tasks. The new backbone experiments use existing data and do not expand task or environment coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 removes the separate zero-shot ViNT entry, although that comparator remains in other analyses. New Appendix Table IV includes ViNT as an architecture comparator alongside encoder variants. GNM, ViNT, NoMaD, and GPT-4o remain the principal comparison methods.

E3.justification: The central offline comparison changes substantially: Table 1 replaces AOE(5) reporting with L2 distance and changes GNM and NoMaD from zero-shot to fine-tuned settings. New Table IV compares architectures after 2000 hours of video pretraining and expert fine-tuning. Existing data splits and real-world testing procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix Table IV adds backbone/architecture sensitivity analysis and accompanying inference-speed comparisons. Existing component ablations, prediction-horizon analysis, data/model scaling studies, training-loss curves, and qualitative success/failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both retain the stated 8–14 real-world trials per case. V3 adds no seed information, repeated-training counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or new uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds L2 scores and replaces zero-shot GNM/NoMaD results with fine-tuned results; for example, GNM scenario-mean MAOE changes from 27.07 degrees to 16.2 degrees under different training conditions. Appendix Table IV and the 1.7 versus 20 fps measurements are new. These substantially extend the reported comparisons, while Table 2's real-world success rates remain identical.

T1.justification: The navigation formulation and Equations (1)–(4), defining orientation metrics and training losses, are unchanged. Adding L2 evaluation introduces no new mathematical derivation, assumption, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same central claims about scalable imitation learning from web videos and improved urban navigation. V3 explicitly mentions data scaling in its contribution list, but that claim already appears in v1's experiments and conclusion.

C2.justification: V3 adds the interpretation that accuracy is relatively insensitive to backbone choice, enabling faster deployment. Section 5 reframes location sensitivity from a limitation of simple processing to noise from naive iPhone location inputs, and suggests better GPS hardware as an additional remedy.

D1.justification: V3 adds RTX 3060 inference information and ACO initialization details, but removes the exact GPT-4o prompt shown in v1's Appendix Figure III. The introduction's future code/data release promise is also removed; project/data-source links and Table II's training hyperparameters remain.

R1.justification: V3 adds references to SelfD, GPT-4V for robotics, and ACO. Related work explicitly contrasts SelfD's preference for BEV pseudo-labeling with CityWalker's use of visual odometry at scale; the broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Changes comprise brief related-work and backbone additions, revised contribution and limitation wording, an author-name/contact correction, and small language fixes. The main section sequence and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 changes metric rows and removes a comparator block. V3 adds Appendix Table IV, removes the prompt figure, and repositions retained appendix material. The qualitative Figure IV becomes Figure III with unchanged examples; other principal illustrations and plots are retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, fine-tuning two additional baselines, adding L2 evaluation, and testing architecture/runtime alternatives modestly strengthen empirical scrutiny and practical usefulness. These gains outweigh limited losses: v3 removes the GPT-4o prompt and leaves Section 4.2's broad superiority claim inconsistent with some new L2 scores, such as crowd errors of 1.12 m for CityWalker versus 0.66 m for ViNT.
